title: Laws of indices
intro: Read this before the first questions. The same rules come back in surds and logarithms.

blocks.title: what an index is
blocks.body: $a^m=a\times a\times\cdots\times a$ ($m$ times). $a$ is the **base** and $m$ is the **index** (also called the power or exponent).

blocks.title: the usual slips
items: Same base: **add** the indices when multiplying, **subtract** when dividing.
A negative index gives a **reciprocal**, not a negative number: $5^{-1}=\frac15$.
$a^{p}b^{p}=(ab)^{p}$ only works when the **indices are equal**.

blocks.body: For a fractional index, take the root first, then the power: $27^{2/3}=(\sqrt[3]{27})^{2}=9$.

blocks.title: typed answers
blocks.body: Type powers with `^`: $x^{10}$ is `x^10`. Products of letters are written side by side: `x^5 y^8 z`.
